what_this_is: Whether each hand-proposed HYP-05 candidate (see hand_curated_candidates.py -- proposals from general knowledge, not extracted from a filing) actually appears, by name, in a real 10-K filed by its proposed anchor -- WITH a readable sentence of context actually confirming it, not just a raw search-index hit. `filed_mention_confirmed: true` requires both: efts.sec.gov reported a hit AND this script independently located the name inside the fetched document text. A hit with no readable context (common for pre-2001 filings with non-standard archive paths, or 10-Ks whose indexed document is a PDF that strip_markup cannot parse) is marked `search_hit_found_but_context_unreadable: true` and kept OUT of filed_mention_confirmed and out of the linkage edges file -- a real index hit is not the same claim as a readable, checkable sentence. A THIRD case: readable context that names the counterparty for a reason that has nothing to do with a business relationship (a stock-performance-graph benchmark-index table; a director/officer's prior-employment biography) is marked `context_rejected_as_non_relationship_evidence: true` -- see classify_context() in this module, and its dedicated test, for exactly which patterns and why. Confirmation of the NAME does NOT independently confirm the claimed direction (competitor/supplier/customer) -- read `context` for that.
what_this_is_not: Curation. Confirmation here only gates entry into the existing name-resolution + point-in-time market-cap pipeline (run_hyp05_peer_name_search.py, run_hyp05_peer_market_cap.py) -- no edge here is a production linkage-map row.
unconfirmed_is_not_a_negative: A candidate with no full-text hit may still be a real relationship that was simply never named in a 10-K, or named using different wording than proposed here. filed_mention_confirmed: false means unconfirmed by this evidence standard, not disproven.
